title: Balloon Burst Maximum
statement:
A row of balloons has a number printed on each: `balloons[i]` is on balloon `i`. When you burst balloon `i` you earn `left * balloons[i] * right` coins, where `left` and `right` are the numbers on the balloons **currently** next to it. After it bursts, those two neighbours become neighbours of each other. If a neighbour does not exist (you are at an edge), use `1` in its place.

Burst every balloon, in the best order, and return the most coins you can earn.

hints.nudge: Thinking about which balloon to burst FIRST is hard, because the neighbours keep changing. What is easy to say about the balloon you burst LAST in a stretch?
hints.pattern: Interval DP: best[l][r] = most coins from bursting everything strictly between positions l and r, choosing which balloon k bursts last.
hints.walkthrough: Try the order of bursts directly and you get n! possibilities. Turn the question around: in the stretch strictly between two positions l and r, pick the balloon k that bursts LAST. At that moment everything else between l and r is gone, so its neighbours are exactly l and r and it earns nums[l] * nums[k] * nums[r]. The balloons left of k and right of k were burst earlier, and they cannot interfere with each other because k was still standing between them: they are two independent smaller problems, best[l][k] and best[k][r]. Pad the row with a 1 on each side, fill the table by increasing gap length, and the answer is best[0][n+1]. O(n^3) time, O(n^2) memory.
